summary: The figures an indicator actually recorded, one for each reporting period.
example: Quality pass rate: 63 percent in November 2025, 64.5 in February 2026, 66 in May 2026.
definition: The figures a KPI recorded, one for each period, such as each month or season. The KPI says what is measured; the readings say what the number was. A period with no reading has not been read yet; it is not zero. Readings are not the KPI, its baseline or its target.

/spec/kpi.guide: The KPI these figures belong to.

/metadata/name.guide: The KPI's name followed by the word readings.

poor.why: Keep all years in one list; do not split it by year.

/spec/readings.guide: One figure for each period that has been read. Skip periods nobody has read. To correct a figure, edit it; do not add a second one.

/spec/readings/-/period.guide: The month the period ends, as YYYY-MM. For a season from December to February, enter February.
good: 2026-02, for the season from December to February
2026-03, for March on the monthly cycle

poor.text: 2025-12, for the season from December to February
poor.why: That is the month the period starts. Use the month it ends.

poor.text: 2026-02, entered a second time with a corrected value
poor.why: Each period has one figure. Correct the existing one, and mark it provisional if it may still change.

/spec/readings/-/value.guide: The figure for this period, as a plain number.

poor.why: Leave out the unit; the KPI already has it.
Zero is a real figure. Leave out a period with no figure.

/spec/readings/-/provisional.guide: Mark this if the figure may still change. Clear it once the figure is final.

/spec/readings/-/note.guide: Anything that explains this figure, such as a change in how it was counted or a period only partly collected.
good: The wet season brought more bruising than the standard allows for; the method did not change.

poor.why: Say what made it different and whether the way it was counted changed.
